applicability: Redesigns of products whose look and feel is part of what users recognise and trust
contraindications: Operator approved a rebrand or marked the look for replacement

rules.recommendation: Always propose structural evolution (simpler navigation, clearer journeys, visible active states, a stronger hierarchy) and express it in the existing character: the same fonts, colours and chrome, used by context. Keeping the look is never a reason to keep the structure as it is.
contraindications: Operator approved a rebrand or marked the look for replacement
Swap typography and palette as the first step of every redesign

rules.recommendation: Carry intentional look-and-feel traits (period chrome, archival typography, a signature colour) into the redesign so it stays recognisable, and rebuild the layout and flows around them; character decides how new elements look, not whether they improve.
contraindications: Operator approved a rebrand or marked the look for replacement

rules.recommendation: In catalog, archive and library products, dense listings and visible metadata are often part of the character and of the task; make them easier to use with grouping, sorting, filters and wayfinding instead of trading density for whitespace without task evidence.
contraindications: Pad every listing into spacious tiles for a modern look

rules.recommendation: Modernise in the product's own visual language, drawn from the recorded identity and the audience, rather than falling back to a generic SaaS template (large rounded panels, soft shadows, a stock sans-serif, a gradient hero).
contraindications: Operator approved a rebrand or marked the look for replacement
Apply the same rounded-panel template to every product

rules.recommendation: Before restyling, record which traits are intentional, incidental or unknown, with evidence, and for each kept trait write how it gets easier to use without losing its style; an intentional trait nobody has decided on keeps its style and still evolves.
